newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets close firmer on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets close firmer on short covering.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (JUN) 92.84 (PREV 92.72) 90-DAYS 7.02 (PREV 7.10)
OVERNIGHT CASH 6.50 PCT (PREV 6.30) US 5-YR 6.50 (PREV 6.53)
* NZ rates fall back after Monday's sell-off
* Higher TWI, eurobond issue buoys short end and mid curve
* 90-days seen settling around 7.0 pct
New Zealand debt securities closed stronger on Tuesday, bouncing back from a sell-off on Monday after the Reserve Bank called for somewhat firmer monetary conditions.
"It's certainly a bid tone, rates are down, but there's a bit of feeling we won't race on down, that it was just a snap reaction yesterday and things have settled down," a dealer said.
The key 90-day bank bill rate, which spiked 26 points higher on Monday following the RBNZ statement, recouped eight points to end at 7.02 percent.
Dealers said the currency's higher Trade-Weighted Index and a eurobond issued overnight were helping to buoy the short to mid-dated maturities.
One said the NZ$100 million two-year eurokiwi announced by Hypo-Bank showed New Zealand rates were still attractive to overseas investors.

On Monday, interest rates and the Kiwi jumped higher when the Reserve Bank said overall monetary conditions "appeared to be settling at levels somewhat too low to be consistent with the intended stance of monetary conditions".
However, the bank is still widely expected to allow conditions to ease a little in its June Monetary Policy Statement (MPS).
"The market obviously pulled back yesterdy and people have decided it was worth buying into," said another dealer.

Yields across the curve fell between eight and 11 points. "With yesterday's move, unless the TWI bounces quite strongly, it's pretty hard to see our short rates rallying too far from current levels, but possibly you might see a little bit more downside in the mid and long bond yields based on further strength offshore," the dealer added.
The 90-days were expected to settle around 7.0 percent until the June MPS.

"One gets the feeling that in the 90-days, around that 7.0 percent is the level the market is inclined to settle into, rather than move strongly away from. The actual investor demand under 7.0 percent tends to be very limited," a trader said.
-- Matthew Brockett, Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 473-3736
